title: Saved mouse visual spectra do not separate subject dimension from subject alignment in rank-20 and rank-30 models
abstract: We test what pooled mouse visual response spectra identify about geometry inside a mouse. For any positive rank-K spectrum with K no greater than subject count M, an established frame theorem permits M unit-rank, unit-trace subject kernels with that pooled spectrum. We construct this alternative for the first 20 and 30 saved values from Allen Neuropixels and two-photon aggregate spectra. All 1,400 draw checks pass with errors below 2e-14. Thus these retained pooled spectra do not separate within-subject dimension from between-subject image-pattern alignment. We give an exact kernel-moment decomposition and a four-partition unbiased estimator under independent zero-mean repeat noise and fixed scales. Simulations pass the independent-noise check and fail a shared-noise control. This is a model and method result, not evidence that alignment caused the biological hierarchy trend. It does not explain the full spectrum with rank-one subjects or remove the source within-mouse evidence. Licensed aggregate inputs, original code, proofs, figures, hashes and offline reproduction steps are included.

display.caption: Retained-spectrum models and noise checks. Rank-one model subjects reproduce pooled concentration. Four independent repeat groups remove kernel-moment bias under the tested assumptions.
